title: "Watching Live: The Master Checklist and Anticipation"
subtitle: "Twenty seconds between snaps, nine questions in the right order, the full catalogue of tells, and a prediction with a number on it."
description: "The course's live-watching protocol, assembled: the master pre-snap checklist (situation, personnel, formation and strength, motion response, box, shell, leverage, pressure tells, prediction) and how to run it inside one play clock; what each step is worth, measured on 2024–2025 nflverse and FTN data; the full tells catalogue for both sides of the ball; stated confidence and layered predictions; a complete 2025 NFC Championship Game drive by the Seattle Seahawks, called snap by snap; and the upgraded prediction log that the next chapter scores."
glossary:
  "Master pre-snap checklist": "The course's complete pre-snap routine, run in the same order before every snap in roughly twenty seconds: situation, personnel, formation and strength, motion response, box, shell, leverage, pressure tells, and finally a prediction. The order follows when each clue becomes visible and which answers the later clues depend on."
  "Stated confidence": "The probability you attach to a prediction before the snap, said or written as a number (55%, 70%, 90%) rather than a feeling, so that it can be scored later. A well-judged 70% call comes true about seven times in ten."

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Show the Python (shared drawing helpers for this chapter)"
#| output: false
import os
import re
import tempfile
import textwrap
import logging

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, FancyArrowPatch, Rectangle, Circle, Patch
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

from gridiron import Play, Player, offense, defense, routes as r, style, draw_marker, show_animation

logging.getLogger("matplotlib.font_manager").setLevel(logging.ERROR)
style.apply()
PDF = os.environ.get("RTG_FORMAT", "").lower() in ("pdf", "typst", "print")
FIELD_W = 160 / 3
LOOK = "#0f7a55"           # "look here" badges (a darker step of the aqua highlight)
NEW_TINT = "#dcefe6"       # rows that are new in this chapter on the card


def pct(x, nd=0):
    """0.613 -> '61%'."""
    return f"{100 * x:.{nd}f}%"


def blank(ax):
    ax.set_axis_off()
    ax.grid(False)


def no_numbers(ax):
    """Remove the painted yard-line numbers (they sit where wide receivers and corners stand)."""
    for t in list(ax.texts):
        if t.get_alpha() == 0.55:
            t.remove()


def badge(ax, x, y, n, color=LOOK, r=1.15, fs=7.5, z=15):
    """A numbered circle in plot coordinates (equal-aspect axes only)."""
    ax.add_patch(Circle((x, y), r, fc=color, ec="white", lw=0.8, zorder=z))
    ax.text(x, y, str(n), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=fs, color="white", fontweight="bold", zorder=z + 1)


def fbadge(fld, play, n, at, **kw):
    """A numbered badge at alignment coordinates (d, w)."""
    x, y = fld.xy(*play.to_abs(*at))
    badge(fld.ax, float(x), float(y), n, **kw)


def tag(fld, play, text, at, fs=7.0, ha="center", color=style.INK, bold=False, ec=style.BASELINE):
    """A boxed label at alignment coordinates (d, w), drawn above the players."""
    x, y = fld.xy(*play.to_abs(*at))
    fld.ax.text(x, y, text, ha=ha, va="center", fontsize=fs, color=color, zorder=14, linespacing=1.12,
                fontweight="bold" if bold else "normal",
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.25", fc=style.SURFACE, ec=ec, lw=0.6))


def scorebug(fld, play, lines, at, fs=6.6, ha="left"):
    """A small dark scorebug box at (d, w)."""
    x, y = fld.xy(*play.to_abs(*at))
    fld.ax.text(x, y, "\n".join(lines), ha=ha, va="center", fontsize=fs, color="white", zorder=16,
                linespacing=1.25, fontweight="bold",
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.35", fc="#2b2b2b", ec="none"))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ print stand-ins for animations
def snapshot(play, t, ax, lateral, window, notes=(), trails=True):
    """Everyone where he is at time t, with faint trails of where he has been and the ball in flight."""
    pos = {k: play.position(k, t) for k in play.players}
    moved = [pl.moved(d=float(pos[k][0]), w=float(pos[k][1])) for k, pl in play.players.items()]
    q = Play([m for m in moved if m.side == "off"], [m for m in moved if m.side == "def"],
             los=play.los, ball_y=play.ball_y, to_go=play.to_go)
    q.highlights = dict(play.highlights)
    for n in notes:
        q.note(*n)
    fld = q.draw(ax=ax, lateral=lateral, window=window, title=False)
    no_numbers(fld.ax)
    ppy = fld.pts_per_yard()
    P = lambda d, w: fld.xy(*play.to_abs(d, w))  # noqa: E731
    t0 = play._compile()[1]
    if trails:
        for k, pl in play.players.items():
            if pl.pos in ("LT", "LG", "C", "RG", "RT"):
                continue
            pts = np.array([play.position(k, tt) for tt in np.linspace(t0, t, 40)])
            if np.ptp(pts[:, 0]) + np.ptp(pts[:, 1]) < 0.4:
                continue
            xs, ys = P(pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1])
            col = style.OFFENSE if pl.side == "off" else style.DEFENSE
            ls = "-" if pl.side == "off" else (0, (3, 2))
            ax.plot(xs, ys, color=col, lw=1.0, alpha=0.5, ls=ls, zorder=3)
    bx, by = P(*play.ball_position(t))
    thrown = False
    for kind, _, t_rel in play.ball_events:
        if kind == "pass" and t > t_rel:
            thrown = True
            sx, sy = P(*play.ball_position(t_rel))
            ax.add_patch(FancyArrowPatch((float(sx), float(sy)), (float(bx), float(by)), arrowstyle="-|>",
                                         mutation_scale=8, color=style.BALL, lw=1.3, ls=(0, (2, 1.5)), zorder=9))
    if thrown:
        draw_marker(ax, float(bx), float(by), "ball", "", ppy)   # before the throw the QB has it: no icon on him
    elif t > 0:
        for who, tgt in play.reads:                               # the quarterback's eyes, until he throws
            (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = P(*play.position(who, t)), P(*play.position(tgt, t))
            ax.plot([float(x0), float(x1)], [float(y0), float(y1)], color=style.THIRD, lw=1.2, ls=(0, (4, 2)),
                    zorder=4)
    return fld


def strip(play, times, labels, lateral, window, notes_at=None, ncols=2, width_in=6.5):
    """The print version of an animation: one panel per moment, each titled with what to see."""
    n = len(times)
    nrows = int(np.ceil(n / ncols))
    pw = width_in / ncols
    h = nrows * (pw * (window[1] - window[0]) / abs(lateral[1] - lateral[0]) + 0.36)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows, ncols, figsize=(width_in, h), squeeze=False)
    for ax in axes.flat[n:]:
        ax.axis("off")
    for i, (ax, t, lab) in enumerate(zip(axes.flat, times, labels)):
        snapshot(play, t, ax, lateral, window, notes=(notes_at or {}).get(i, ()))
        ax.set_title(lab, fontsize=8.2, color=style.INK, loc="left")
    fig.tight_layout(h_pad=0.5, w_pad=0.4)
    return fig


def animate_or_strip(play, times, labels, lateral, window, notes_at=None):
    """Video on the web, a titled frame strip in print."""
    if PDF:
        strip(play, times, labels, lateral, window, notes_at=notes_at)
        plt.show()
    else:
        show_animation(play, times=times)


def protect(p, linemen=("LT", "LG", "C", "RG", "RT")):
    """Five linemen set back into pass protection."""
    for k in linemen:
        p.block(k, pts=[(-1.2, 0.0)])


def engage(p, rushers, speed=2.0):
    """Rushers who run into the protection (enough to show a pass rush, no more)."""
    for k in rushers:
        p.rush(k, pts=[(-1.6, 0.0)], speed=speed)
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Show the Python (data: nflverse play-by-play, participation and FTN charting, 2024–2025)"
#| output: false
from gridiron.data import pbp, nfl

PCOLS = ["season_type", "game_id", "play_id", "posteam", "defteam", "play_type", "down", "ydstogo",
         "yardline_100", "pass", "half_seconds_remaining", "score_differential", "qtr", "fixed_drive", "time",
         "yrdln", "desc", "yards_gained", "posteam_score", "defteam_score", "air_yards", "yards_after_catch",
         "qb_dropback", "run_location", "pass_location"]


def load_season(season):
    """Runs and dropbacks with FTN charting (alignment, motion, tempo, rushers) and participation
    (personnel, box count, coverage label) attached."""
    d = pbp([season], columns=PCOLS)
    d = d[d.play_type.isin(["pass", "run"]) & d.down.notna()].copy()
    f = nfl().load_ftn_charting([season]).to_pandas()
    f = f.rename(columns={"nflverse_game_id": "game_id", "nflverse_play_id": "play_id"})
    f["play_id"] = f.play_id.astype(float)
    f = f[["game_id", "play_id", "starting_hash", "qb_location", "n_offense_backfield", "is_motion", "is_no_huddle",
           "is_play_action", "is_screen_pass", "n_pass_rushers", "n_blitzers", "read_thrown",
           "is_qb_out_of_pocket"]]
    p = nfl().load_participation([season]).to_pandas()
    p = p.rename(columns={"nflverse_game_id": "game_id"})
    p["play_id"] = p.play_id.astype(float)
    p = p[["game_id", "play_id", "offense_personnel", "defense_personnel", "defenders_in_box",
           "defense_coverage_type", "defense_man_zone_type", "time_to_throw", "was_pressure", "route"]]
    d["play_id"] = d.play_id.astype(float)
    return d.merge(f, on=["game_id", "play_id"], how="left").merge(p, on=["game_id", "play_id"], how="left")


def count_pos(s, keys):
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        return np.nan
    c = {k: int(v) for v, k in re.findall(r"(\d+) ([A-Z]+)", s)}
    return sum(c.get(k, 0) for k in keys)


def pers_code(s):
    """FTN-era personnel string ('1 C, 2 G, 1 QB, 1 RB, 2 T, 1 TE, 3 WR') -> '11'."""
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        return "na"
    c = {k: int(v) for v, k in re.findall(r"(\d+) ([A-Z]+)", s)}
    code = f"{c.get('RB', 0) + c.get('FB', 0)}{c.get('TE', 0)}"
    return code if code in ("10", "11", "12", "13", "21", "22", "01", "02") else "other"


def features(d):
    d = d.copy()
    dist = pd.cut(d.ydstogo, [0, 1, 2, 3, 6, 10, 99], labels=["1", "2", "3", "4-6", "7-10", "11+"]).astype(str)
    d["dd"] = d.down.astype(int).astype(str) + "_" + dist
    d["zone"] = pd.cut(d.yardline_100, [0, 5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100],
                       labels=["g5", "g10", "rz", "o40", "mid", "own40", "own20"]).astype(str)
    d["score"] = pd.cut(d.score_differential, [-99, -9, -1, 0, 8, 99],
                        labels=["d9+", "d1-8", "tie", "u1-8", "u9+"]).astype(str)
    d["late"] = np.where(d.half_seconds_remaining <= 120, "late", "no")
    d["q4score"] = np.where(d.qtr >= 4, "q4", "no") + d["score"]
    d["pers"] = d.offense_personnel.map(pers_code)
    backs = d.n_offense_backfield.fillna(-1).clip(upper=2).astype(int).astype(str)
    d["formation"] = d.qb_location.fillna("na").astype(str) + backs
    d["motion"] = d.is_motion.fillna(False).astype(bool).astype(str)
    d["tempo"] = d.is_no_huddle.fillna(False).astype(bool).astype(str)
    d["box"] = pd.cut(d.defenders_in_box.fillna(-1), [-2, 0, 5, 6, 7, 99],
                      labels=["na", "5-", "6", "7", "8+"]).astype(str)
    d["dbs"] = d.defense_personnel.map(lambda s: count_pos(s, ("CB", "FS", "SS", "S", "DB")))
    return d


# The checklist steps that can be measured in public data, in checklist order
STEPS = [("Situation", ["dd", "zone", "score", "late", "q4score"]),
         ("+ Personnel", ["pers"]),
         ("+ Formation", ["formation"]),
         ("+ Motion and tempo", ["motion", "tempo"]),
         ("+ Box count", ["box"])]


def design(d, cats, levels=None):
    if levels is None:
        levels = {c: sorted(d[c].unique()) for c in cats}
    cols = [np.ones(len(d))]
    for c in cats:
        for lv in levels[c][1:]:
            cols.append((d[c].values == lv).astype(float))
    return np.column_stack(cols), levels


def fit(X, y, lam=1.0, iters=30):
    """Ridge-penalised logistic regression by Newton's method (numpy only)."""
    w = np.zeros(X.shape[1])
    for _ in range(iters):
        p = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-X @ w))
        H = X.T @ (X * (p * (1 - p))[:, None]) + lam * np.eye(X.shape[1])
        w -= np.linalg.solve(H, X.T @ (p - y) + lam * w)
    return w


def nested(train):
    models, cats = [], []
    for name, cs in STEPS:
        cats = cats + cs
        X, lv = design(train, cats)
        models.append((name, list(cats), lv, fit(X, train["pass"].values.astype(float))))
    return models


def predict(model, d):
    _, cats, lv, w = model
    X, _ = design(d, cats, lv)
    return 1 / (1 + np.exp(-X @ w))


S24 = features(load_season(2024))
S25 = features(load_season(2025))
TR = S24[S24.season_type == "REG"]
TE = S25[S25.season_type == "REG"]

# What each step is worth: learn on 2024, score on 2025
MODELS = nested(TR)
WORTH = [dict(step="Always guess pass", acc=float(TE["pass"].mean()), hi=np.nan, hi_acc=np.nan)]
for m in MODELS:
    p_ = predict(m, TE)
    y_ = TE["pass"].values
    right = (p_ >= 0.5) == y_
    hi = np.maximum(p_, 1 - p_) >= 0.8
    WORTH.append(dict(step=m[0], acc=float(right.mean()), hi=float(hi.mean()), hi_acc=float(right[hi].mean())))
W = {w_["step"]: w_ for w_ in WORTH}

# Confidence bands after the first three steps (situation, personnel, formation)
pF = predict(MODELS[2], TE)
cF = np.maximum(pF, 1 - pF)
rF = (pF >= 0.5) == TE["pass"].values
BANDS = []
for lo, hi_ in [(0.5, 0.6), (0.6, 0.7), (0.7, 0.8), (0.8, 0.9), (0.9, 1.01)]:
    m_ = (cF >= lo) & (cF < hi_)
    BANDS.append(dict(lo=lo, hi=min(hi_, 1.0), share=float(m_.mean()), acc=float(rF[m_].mean()),
                      conf=float(cF[m_].mean())))


def prate(mask):
    return float(TE.loc[mask, "pass"].mean())


RATE = dict(
    all=prate(TE.down > 0),
    first10=prate((TE.down == 1) & (TE.ydstogo == 10)),
    third7=prate((TE.down == 3) & TE.ydstogo.between(7, 10)),
    third46gun11=prate((TE.down == 3) & TE.ydstogo.between(4, 6) & (TE.pers == "11") & (TE.qb_location == "S")),
    third3gun=prate((TE.down == 3) & (TE.ydstogo == 3) & (TE.qb_location == "S")),
    third12uc=prate((TE.down == 3) & TE.ydstogo.between(1, 2) & (TE.qb_location == "U")),
    third12gun=prate((TE.down == 3) & TE.ydstogo.between(1, 2) & (TE.qb_location == "S")),
    second12=prate((TE.down == 2) & TE.ydstogo.between(1, 2)),
    second12gun11=prate((TE.down == 2) & TE.ydstogo.between(1, 2) & (TE.pers == "11") & (TE.qb_location == "S")),
    second12gun11nh=prate((TE.down == 2) & TE.ydstogo.between(1, 2) & (TE.pers == "11")
                          & (TE.qb_location == "S") & (TE.tempo == "True")),
    first21uc=prate((TE.down == 1) & (TE.ydstogo == 10) & (TE.pers == "21") & (TE.qb_location == "U")),
    first21uc8=prate((TE.down == 1) & (TE.ydstogo == 10) & (TE.pers == "21") & (TE.qb_location == "U")
                     & (TE["box"] == "8+")),
    first12uc=prate((TE.down == 1) & (TE.ydstogo == 10) & (TE.pers == "12") & (TE.qb_location == "U")),
    empty=prate(TE["formation"] == "S0"),
    gun=prate(TE.qb_location == "S"), pistol=prate(TE.qb_location == "P"), uc=prate(TE.qb_location == "U"),
    nohuddle=prate(TE.tempo == "True"),
)
LOOK6 = ((TE.down == 2) & TE.ydstogo.between(1, 2) & (TE.pers == "11") & (TE.qb_location == "S")
         & (TE.n_offense_backfield == 1) & (TE.motion == "True") & (TE["box"] == "6"))
RATE["look6"] = prate(LOOK6)
N_LOOK6 = int(LOOK6.sum())
N_SECOND12NH = int(((TE.down == 2) & TE.ydstogo.between(1, 2) & (TE.pers == "11") & (TE.qb_location == "S")
                    & (TE.tempo == "True")).sum())
N_FIRST21UC8 = int(((TE.down == 1) & (TE.ydstogo == 10) & (TE.pers == "21") & (TE.qb_location == "U")
                    & (TE["box"] == "8+")).sum())

# Rushers and coverage on dropbacks (2025 regular season)
DBK = S25[(S25.season_type == "REG") & (S25.qb_dropback == 1) & (S25.n_pass_rushers > 0)].copy()
DBK["five"] = (DBK.n_pass_rushers >= 5).astype(float)
COV = DBK[DBK.defense_man_zone_type.isin(["MAN_COVERAGE", "ZONE_COVERAGE"])].copy()
COV["man"] = (COV.defense_man_zone_type == "MAN_COVERAGE").astype(float)


def rush5(mask):
    return float(DBK.loc[mask, "five"].mean())


RUSH = dict(all=rush5(DBK.down > 0), third46=rush5((DBK.down == 3) & DBK.ydstogo.between(4, 6)),
            third7=rush5((DBK.down == 3) & DBK.ydstogo.between(7, 10)))
MAN_ALL = float(COV["man"].mean())
MAN_RZ = float(COV.loc[COV.yardline_100 <= 20, "man"].mean())
MAN_OPEN = float(COV.loc[COV.yardline_100 > 20, "man"].mean())


def uc_habits(T):
    """How often a team lines up under center, throws from there, and makes those throws play-action."""
    U = T[T.qb_location == "U"]
    return dict(share=float((T.qb_location == "U").mean()), pass_=float(U["pass"].mean()),
                pa=float(U.loc[U["pass"] == 1, "is_play_action"].mean()))


UC_LG, UC_LA = uc_habits(TE), uc_habits(TE[TE.posteam == "LA"])
M12 = (TE.down == 1) & (TE.pers == "12") & (TE.qb_location == "U")
RATE["first12uc_sea"] = prate(M12 & (TE.posteam == "SEA"))
RATE["first12uc_all"] = prate(M12)
N_12UC_SEA = int((M12 & (TE.posteam == "SEA")).sum())

# Field or boundary? FTN's hash is from the offense's view (screens go to the wide side, away from it)
HSH = TE[TE.starting_hash.isin(["L", "R"])]
TO_FIELD = (((HSH.starting_hash == "L") & (HSH.run_location.eq("right") | HSH.pass_location.eq("right")))
            | ((HSH.starting_hash == "R") & (HSH.run_location.eq("left") | HSH.pass_location.eq("left"))))
WIDE = HSH.run_location.isin(["left", "right"]) | HSH.pass_location.isin(["left", "right"])
SCR = WIDE & (HSH.is_screen_pass == True)  # noqa: E712
RUNW = WIDE & (HSH.play_type == "run")
FIELD = dict(screen=float(TO_FIELD[SCR].mean()), run=float(TO_FIELD[RUNW].mean()))


def brier(c, q):
    """Expected Brier score per call when you say c and the call comes true at rate q."""
    return q * (1 - c) ** 2 + (1 - q) * c ** 2


def buckets(d):
    out = pd.DataFrame(index=d.index)
    dist = pd.cut(d.ydstogo, [0, 3, 6, 99], labels=["1-3", "4-6", "7+"]).astype(str)
    out["b_dd"] = d.down.astype(int).clip(upper=3).astype(str) + "_" + dist
    out["b_rz"] = np.where(d.yardline_100 <= 20, "rz", "open")
    out["b_db"] = d.dbs.fillna(5).clip(4, 6).astype(int).astype(str)
    return out


for t_ in (DBK, COV):
    t_[["b_dd", "b_rz", "b_db"]] = buckets(t_)


def lookup(table, col, row, nmin=60):
    """Base rate for this down-distance, field zone and number of DBs, backing off to coarser cells."""
    for keys in (("b_dd", "b_rz", "b_db"), ("b_dd", "b_rz"), ("b_dd",)):
        m_ = np.ones(len(table), bool)
        for k in keys:
            m_ &= table[k].values == row[k]
        if m_.sum() >= nmin:
            return float(table.loc[m_, col].mean())
    return float(table[col].mean())


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the film-room drive
DRV = S25[(S25.game_id == "2025_21_LA_SEA") & (S25.posteam == "SEA") & (S25.fixed_drive == 15)]
DRV = DRV.sort_values("play_id").reset_index(drop=True)
TRACE = nested(pd.concat([TR, TE]))           # trained on the 2024 and 2025 regular seasons
for i_, m in enumerate(TRACE):
    DRV[f"p{i_}"] = predict(m, DRV)
DRV["p"] = DRV[f"p{len(TRACE) - 1}"]


def conf_of(p):
    return int(np.clip(5 * round(100 * max(p, 1 - p) / 5), 50, 90))


DRV["call"] = np.where(DRV.p >= 0.5, "Pass", "Run")
DRV["conf"] = DRV.p.map(conf_of)
bk = buckets(DRV)
DRV["p_man"] = [lookup(COV, "man", bk.loc[i_]) for i_ in DRV.index]
DRV["p_five"] = [lookup(DBK, "five", bk.loc[i_]) for i_ in DRV.index]
DRV["cov_call"] = np.where(DRV.p_man >= 0.5, "man", "zone")
DRV["cov_conf"] = DRV.p_man.map(conf_of)
DRV["rush_call"] = np.where(DRV.p_five >= 0.5, "5+", "4")
DRV["rush_conf"] = DRV.p_five.map(conf_of)
DRV["is_pass"] = DRV["pass"] == 1
DRV["hit"] = (DRV.call == "Pass") == DRV.is_pass
DRV["cov_hit"] = np.where(DRV.is_pass, (DRV.cov_call == "man") == (DRV.defense_man_zone_type == "MAN_COVERAGE"), np.nan)
DRV["rush_hit"] = np.where(DRV.is_pass, (DRV.rush_call == "5+") == (DRV.n_pass_rushers >= 5), np.nan)
RESULT = {2550: "Holani run, +3", 2572: "Walker run, −2", 2594: "Kupp catch, +12 (1st)",
          2619: "Walker run, +11 (1st)", 2641: "Holani catch, +9", 2666: "Smith-Njigba screen, +12 (1st)",
          2691: "Play-action, Barner +7", 2716: "Incomplete to Bobo", 2739: "Kupp, 13-yard TD"}
DRV["result"] = DRV.play_id.map(lambda x: RESULT[int(x)])
D = DRV.set_index(DRV.index + 1)           # D.loc[3] is the third snap of the drive
N_HIT = int(DRV.hit.sum())
N_L2 = int(np.nansum(DRV.cov_hit) + np.nansum(DRV.rush_hit))
N_L2_ALL = int(2 * DRV.is_pass.sum())
N_COV = int(np.nansum(DRV.cov_hit))
N_RUSH = int(np.nansum(DRV.rush_hit))
N_PASS = int(DRV.is_pass.sum())


Q90 = BANDS[4]["acc"]
BRIER = dict(c90=brier(0.90, Q90), honest=brier(Q90, Q90), c99=brier(0.99, Q90))


def snap_conf(i):
    return f"{D.loc[i, 'call'].lower()}, {D.loc[i, 'conf']}%"
```

**The NFC Championship Game, January 25, 2026.** Third quarter, 8:23 to play, and the Rams have just
pulled within four points. Seattle faces third-and-9 at its own 36, and on a typical broadcast the replay of the run that just
lost two yards would still be rolling as the Seahawks come back to the line: one running back, one
tight end, three receivers, quarterback in the shotgun. The Rams answer with six defensive backs
and only five men near the ball. You have about twenty seconds. Most viewers spend them waiting for
the snap. A coach in the booth spends them asking a set of questions in the same order he asks them
before every snap: *What does the situation demand? Who's on the field? How are they lined up? What
does the defense do when someone moves? How many are in the box? How many are deep? Where is the help?
Is anyone coming?* And then he says out loud what he thinks will happen, and how sure he is. This
chapter puts the whole course into that routine. By the end of it you'll run the same questions in
the same order, and you'll keep score.

**You'll be able to…**

- Run the master pre-snap checklist in about twenty seconds, in order: situation → personnel →
  formation and strength → motion response → box → shell → leverage → pressure tells → prediction,
  and know which steps to keep when the offense goes fast.
- Use the full tells catalogue (linemen's stance and weight, the back's depth and offset, pistol
  against shotgun, receiver splits, the tight end's stance, linebacker depth, defensive back depth
  and leverage, safety width), saying for each what it usually means and why it leaks, and, where public
  data can measure it, how often it lies.
- Say what each step of the checklist is worth, from 2024–2025 data, and why the later steps answer
  different questions from run or pass.
- Make layered predictions (run or pass first, then the coverage family, the rush, where the ball
  goes or which way the run hits), each with a stated confidence between 50% and 90%.
- Follow a complete playoff drive snap by snap the way a coach in the booth does, and keep the log
  that [Film Study](15-02-film-study-and-charting.qmd) will score.

::: {.callout-note title="You'll need"}
This is a Level 5 chapter: it assembles the course rather than adding new schemes. One line on each
piece it leans on hardest:

- **In-game adjustments and tempo** ([In-Game Adjustments, Tempo, and the Sideline Battle](../08-the-chess-match/08-04-in-game-adjustments-and-tempo.qmd)):
  [tempo](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-tempo) is how fast the offense gets to the line and snaps; a
  [hurry-up offense](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-hurry-up-offense) snaps as fast as it can, and the
  [substitution freeze](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-substitution-freeze) means a defense that
  can't match a substitution has to play with the eleven it has. Staffs adjust between series, and the
  play that follows a successful call (the call after the call) often builds on it.
- **The clock and fourth down** ([The Clock, the Two-Minute Drill, and Fourth Down](../10-situational-football/10-04-clock-and-game-management.qmd)):
  in the [two-minute drill](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-two-minute-drill) and the
  [four-minute offense](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-four-minute-offense) the clock decides much of
  the play call, and fourth down is a decision of its own.
- **Tendencies from data** ([Tendencies: PROE, Personnel, Motion, and Coverage from Charting Data](../13-analytics-and-data/13-04-tendencies-proe-and-charting.qmd)):
  [xpass](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-xpass) (expected pass rate) is the chance of a pass given the
  situation alone, and [PROE](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-proe) (pass rate over expected) is how
  much a team throws beyond it. A team's [tendency](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-tendency) is a
  pattern in what it calls from a given situation or look.
- **The habit** ([How to Watch a Broadcast Like You Mean It](../01-foundations/01-06-how-to-watch-a-broadcast.qmd)):
  a [tell](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-tell) is a pre-snap clue that shifts the odds, never a
  guarantee; the [prediction log](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-prediction-log) is your record of
  calls, with a confidence column you've been filling in since Part 1. The "checklist so far" cards at
  the end of [Motion and Shifts](../02-personnel-and-formations/02-06-motion-and-shifts.qmd),
  [Offensive Systems](../04-the-passing-game/04-08-offensive-systems-and-languages.qmd),
  [Disguise and Rotation](../06-pass-coverage/06-06-disguise-rotation-and-split-field.qmd) and
  [Zone Blitzes](../07-pressure/07-03-zone-blitz-and-simulated-pressure.qmd) are the drafts of the
  card this chapter finishes.
:::

## Twenty seconds, a hundred clues

Start with the problem the checklist solves: there's far more to see before a snap than anyone can
see, and very little time. The play clock is 40 seconds, starting the moment the previous play is
whistled dead (25 seconds after some stoppages, such as a timeout or a change of possession).[^clock]
On a broadcast the first part of that is usually spent on replays of the play that just ended. The
offense huddles while its play-caller talks to the quarterback through the helmet radio, which goes
silent with 15 seconds left on the play clock.[^radio] Then the players walk to the line, set, maybe
move someone in motion, and the ball is snapped. A team that huddles spends most of what is left of the
play clock at the line; a team in tempo can snap within a few seconds of setting.

So your budget is roughly twenty seconds, from the moment the scorebug updates to the snap, and the
camera won't show you all of it. Within those twenty seconds, information doesn't arrive all at once.
It arrives in a fixed order, because the game produces it in a fixed order:

```{python}
#| label: fig-clock-budget
#| fig-cap: "Twenty seconds, in order. Top: what a typical huddling offense does with the 40-second play clock (timings vary by team and snap; only the radio cut-off at :15 is a rule). Middle: the nine pre-snap steps of the master checklist, placed where each answer usually becomes visible: the situation during the replay, the personnel as players run on, the formation when the offense sets, the motion and the defense's reply during the cadence, and the box, shell, leverage and pressure in the last few seconds, when the defense finally shows its hand. Bottom: against tempo everything is compressed, so you keep only steps 1, 3, 6 and 9."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 3.55))
blank(ax)
ax.set_xlim(41.6, -1.4)
ax.set_ylim(-0.4, 10.6)
YA = 6.3
ax.plot([40, 0], [YA, YA], color=style.INK_2, lw=1.0, solid_capstyle="butt")
for s in range(40, -1, -5):
    ax.plot([s, s], [YA - 0.17, YA + 0.17], color=style.INK_2, lw=0.9)
    ax.text(s, YA + 0.32, f":{s:02d}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=6.6, color=style.INK_2)
PHASES = [(40, 30, "play over; TV shows\nreplays; players regroup", "#ecebe4"),
          (30, 21, "huddle: the call comes\nin by helmet radio", "#dfeaf7"),
          (21, 15.4, "break, line\nup, set", "#dfeaf7"),
          (14.6, 3, "motion and cadence;\nthe defense shows its look", "#fbe3d7"),
          (3, 0, "snap", "#f6e5b0")]
for a, b, txt, c in PHASES:
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((b, 7.35), a - b, 1.75, fc=c, ec="white", lw=1.6, zorder=2))
    ax.text((a + b) / 2, 8.22, txt, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=6.3, color=style.INK, linespacing=1.1,
            zorder=3)
ax.text(40, 9.75, "A huddling offense, typical timing", ha="left", va="center",
        fontsize=7.6, fontweight="bold", color=style.INK)
ax.text(0, YA - 0.42, "seconds left on the play clock", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=6.3, color=style.INK_2,
        style="italic")
ax.plot([15, 15], [3.3, 9.25], color=style.DEFENSE_DARK, lw=1.0, ls=(0, (3, 2)), zorder=4)
ax.text(14.6, 9.75, "radio off at :15", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=6.6, color=style.DEFENSE_DARK)
STEPS_AT = [(1, 35.0, "situation"), (2, 25.5, "personnel"), (3, 18.0, "formation"), (4, 12.6, "motion"),
            (5, 10.1, "box"), (6, 7.6, "shell"), (7, 5.1, "leverage"), (8, 2.8, "pressure"), (9, 0.5, "call it")]
YC = 4.4
for n, s, lab in STEPS_AT:
    ax.scatter([s], [YC], s=150, color=LOOK, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.8, zorder=5)
    ax.text(s, YC, str(n), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7, color="white", fontweight="bold", zorder=6)
    above = n % 2 == 0
    ax.text(s, YC + (0.62 if above else -0.62), lab, ha="center", va="bottom" if above else "top",
            fontsize=6.4, color=style.INK)
ax.text(40, 5.55, "The checklist, step by step", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=7.6, fontweight="bold",
        color=style.INK)
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((27, 0.55), 13, 1.25, fc="#ecebe4", ec="white", lw=1.6))
ax.text(39.6, 1.18, "against tempo: the snap\ncan come at :25 or sooner", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=6.2,
        color=style.INK, linespacing=1.1)
for n, s in ((1, 25.5), (3, 23.0), (6, 20.5), (9, 18.0)):
    ax.scatter([s], [1.18], s=120, color=LOOK, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.8, zorder=5)
    ax.text(s, 1.18, str(n), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=6.6, color="white", fontweight="bold", zorder=6)
ax.text(16.6, 1.18, "short checklist:\nsituation, formation, shell, call", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=6.2,
        color=style.INK_2, linespacing=1.1)
ax.text(40, 2.45, "No-huddle", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=7.6, fontweight="bold", color=style.INK)
plt.show()
```

That ordering is the first reason the checklist has the shape it has: **each step is asked when its
answer is visible.** There is no point hunting for the safeties while the offense is still in the
huddle; they haven't settled. There is every point in reading the scorebug during the replay, because
the situation is already fixed and nothing else is.

The second reason is less obvious and more important: **each answer changes what the next clue
means.** A safety walking down to eight yards on third-and-9 is a defense guarding the sticks; the same
move on first-and-10 against two tight ends is an eighth man for the run. A receiver tightening his split
means one thing from a team that runs on 70% of its snaps in that look and another from a team that
throws on 70%. Clues aren't independent bits of evidence to be added up. They are answers to questions,
and the questions come in an order. Read the box before you know the personnel, and you'll miscount it.
Read the shell before you know the down, and you won't know what you're looking at.

::: {.callout-important title="Why it exists: a checklist, of all things"}
A checklist sounds like the opposite of expertise. Surely the expert just *sees* it? But the
professions that have to perform under time pressure without missing anything (pilots running a
pre-flight check, surgical teams before an incision) settled long ago on short, ordered checklists, and
not because their people were beginners. A checklist offloads the *remembering* so that attention is
free for the *judging*.[^gawande] The football version works the same way. The quarterback's pre-snap
routine (count the safeties, find the Mike, know where the hot throw goes) is a checklist; so is the
defensive signal-caller's (formation, strength, the check that goes with it). Your job is easier than
theirs, since nobody is about to hit you. But it has the same enemy: the eye goes to the most
interesting thing on the screen (usually the quarterback) and stays there, and the clue that decided
the play happens forty yards away.

What it gives up: a fixed routine is slower than a glance, and on the snaps where the offense hurries
you'll have to cut it short. That's why the card has a short version.
:::

## The master checklist

Here is the card you've been building since Part 2, finished. It is the course's
[**master pre-snap checklist**](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-master-pre-snap-checklist): the complete
pre-snap routine, in the same order before every snap, followed by what to check at the snap and between
snaps.

```{python}
#| label: fig-master-card
#| fig-cap: "The master checklist: the cards from Parts 2, 4, 6 and 7, completed and reordered for speed. Nine pre-snap steps take about twenty seconds in all (the seconds column is a target, not a rule). The shaded lines are what this chapter adds: the full tells catalogue folded into steps 3, 7 and 8, the prediction with a stated confidence as an explicit step, and the between-snaps habits that keep your read of this team, today, up to date. The right-hand column says where each line was taught."
items = [
    ("BEFORE THE SNAP  ·  about 20 seconds", None, None, None, False),
    ("1", "Situation: down, distance, field zone, clock, score, timeouts. Say the base rate: “third-and-9, "
          "pass, 90%-plus”. Two-minute or four-minute?", "3 s", "Part 1, Part 10, 13-04", False),
    ("2", "Personnel: count backs and tight ends as they run on. Did the defense match (base, nickel, dime), "
          "or did tempo freeze it?", "2 s", "02-01, 02-05, 08-04", False),
    ("3", "Formation and strength: under center, gun or pistol; the back's depth and offset; splits; the "
          "tight end's stance and side; any heavy or light hands", "3 s", "Part 2, tells", True),
    ("4", "Motion response: does a defender travel (man), bump (zone) or spin a safety? Still moving at the "
          "snap?", "2 s", "02-06, 06-06", False),
    ("5", "Box: blockers against defenders near the line. Light (6 or fewer) or loaded (8 or more)?", "2 s",
     "02-05, 05-05", False),
    ("6", "Shell: one-high or two-high; each safety's depth and width; who is creeping late?", "2 s",
     "06-01, 06-06", False),
    ("7", "Leverage: corners press or off, inside or outside; linebacker depth; where is the help?", "2 s",
     "04-03, Part 6, tells", True),
    ("8", "Pressure tells: mugs, a safety or nickel walked up, a lineman on his heels. Count the deep "
          "players; where is the hot?", "2 s", "Part 7, 04-02, tells", True),
    ("9", "Call it: run or pass with a stated confidence (50–90%), plus one second-layer call "
          "(coverage, rush or target)", "2 s", "15-01", True),
    ("AT THE SNAP", None, None, None, False),
    ("10", "Linemen's first step (run or pass); did a safety rotate; how many rushed?", "", "Parts 3–7", False),
    ("ONE SECOND AFTER", None, None, None, False),
    ("11", "Middle of the field closed or open; corners squat, bail or trail; where did the ball go?", "",
     "Part 6, 08-01", False),
    ("BETWEEN SNAPS", None, None, None, False),
    ("12", "Log it: call, confidence, the clue that decided it, the result. Five seconds, every snap", "",
     "01-06, 15-01", True),
    ("13", "At each stoppage: update today's tendencies (this personnel, this down); tempo and clock "
           "status; what did they just adjust?", "", "08-04, 10-04, 13-04", True),
]
rows = []
for it in items:
    if it[1] is None:
        rows.append(("head", it[0], 1))
    else:
        lines_ = textwrap.wrap(it[1], 56)
        rows.append(("item", (it[0], lines_, it[2], it[3], it[4]), len(lines_)))
n_lines = sum(h for _, _, h in rows) + 0.18 * sum(k == "item" for k, _, _ in rows) + 4.0
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 0.235 * n_lines))
ax.set_xlim(0, 100)
ax.set_ylim(0, n_lines)
ax.axis("off")
ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((0.8, 0.3), 98.4, n_lines - 0.6, boxstyle="round,pad=0.2,rounding_size=0.8",
                            fc=style.SURFACE, ec=style.BASELINE, lw=1.2))
ax.text(3, n_lines - 1.3, "The master checklist", fontsize=11.5, fontweight="bold", color=style.INK, va="center")
ax.text(97, n_lines - 1.3, "new in the capstone", fontsize=8, color=style.INK, ha="right", va="center",
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc=NEW_TINT, ec="none"))
y = n_lines - 2.9
for kind, payload, h in rows:
    if kind == "head":
        ax.text(3, y, payload, fontsize=8, fontweight="bold", color=style.INK_2, va="center")
        y -= 1.05
        continue
    num, lines_, secs, where, new = payload
    top, bottom = y + 0.47, y - (h - 1) - 0.47
    if new:
        ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((2.2, bottom), 95.6, top - bottom, boxstyle="round,pad=0.05,rounding_size=0.4",
                                    fc=NEW_TINT, ec="none"))
    ax.text(5.0, y, num, fontsize=8.5, fontweight="bold", color=LOOK, va="center", ha="center")
    ax.text(8.2, y, secs, fontsize=6.6, color=style.INK_2, va="center", ha="left")
    for j, ln in enumerate(lines_):
        ax.text(13.0, y - j, ln, fontsize=7.8, color=style.INK, va="center")
    ax.text(97, y, where, fontsize=6.6, color=style.INK_2, va="center", ha="right")
    y -= h + 0.18

```

Compare it with the last draft, the seventeen-line card at the end of
[Zone Blitzes and Simulated Pressure](../07-pressure/07-03-zone-blitz-and-simulated-pressure.qmd), and three
changes stand out. **It's shorter before the snap**: nine steps, not ten, because the protection question
(where is the back, which way will the line slide) has been folded into the pressure step, where you need
it. **The tells have a home**: instead of a separate "run tells" and "pass tells" line, each tell sits in
the step where you'd see it, offensive alignment tells in step 3, defensive depth and leverage in step 7,
pressure tells in step 8. And **the prediction is a step of its own, with a number**: not "I had a feeling
it was a pass" after the fact, but "pass, 80%" before it.

The rest of this section walks the nine pre-snap steps in order. For each: what you're looking at, what it
tells you, and why it sits where it does. None of it is new; what's new is the order and the speed.

### Step 1: situation, the base rate

Down, distance, field zone, clock, score, timeouts. You learned to read the scorebug in five seconds in
[How to Watch a Broadcast](../01-foundations/01-06-how-to-watch-a-broadcast.qmd); Part 10 taught you what
each situation does to the play-caller. The output of step 1 is a number: the **base rate**, how often
offenses throw in this situation before anyone has lined up. That is what
[xpass](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-xpass) measures, and it's the anchor every later step moves.

You don't need a model in your head, just a few landmarks from the 2025 regular season:[^rates]

| Situation | Pass rate, 2025 | What it means for your call |
|:--------------|:-------:|:----------------------|
| All snaps | `{python} pct(RATE["all"])` | "Always pass" is the floor any reader has to beat |
| 1st-and-10 | `{python} pct(RATE["first10"])` | A coin flip until the formation speaks |
| 2nd-and-1 or 2 | `{python} pct(RATE["second12"])` | Mostly runs, but this is where shots happen |
| 3rd-and-1 or 2, under center | `{python} pct(RATE["third12uc"])` | Run, and the formation says so |
| 3rd-and-1 or 2, shotgun | `{python} pct(RATE["third12gun"])` | A genuine coin flip |
| 3rd-and-7 to 10 | `{python} pct(RATE["third7"])` | Pass; spend your seconds on the second layer |
| No-huddle, any down | `{python} pct(RATE["nohuddle"])` | Mostly offenses that are behind; under one in five comes in a two-minute drill |

Two things to say alongside the number. First, **is this a clock situation?** In the
[two-minute drill](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-two-minute-drill) and the
[four-minute offense](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-four-minute-offense) the clock calls half the plays,
and [The Clock, the Two-Minute Drill, and Fourth Down](../10-situational-football/10-04-clock-and-game-management.qmd)
gave you a separate set of questions for them (in bounds or out, timeout or spike, kneel or not). Second,
**does this team break the base rate?** Some offenses throw far more than their situations suggest and some
far less; that is [PROE](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-proe), and
[Tendencies](../13-analytics-and-data/13-04-tendencies-proe-and-charting.qmd) shows how to look it up before
the game (its one-page scouting report is the card to bring). A team with a high PROE moves your 50% first
down toward 55 or 60 before you've seen a thing.

Why it comes first: it's the only clue that's complete during the replay, and it is the biggest single
clue there is. Everything else adjusts it.

### Step 2: personnel, and the match

Count the backs and tight ends as the offense runs on, and watch who runs *off*. The two digits
(11, 12, 21, 13) were the first thing Part 2 taught, because personnel is chosen before the formation: the
play-caller sends in a group, and the group limits what the formation can be. Then glance at the defense's
answer. Did it stay in base, go to nickel, go to dime? A defense in nickel against 12 personnel has a
defensive back where a linebacker usually stands, and the offense will often try to run at him; a defense
in base against 11 personnel has a linebacker who may have to cover a slot receiver, and the offense will
often try to throw at him.

This is also where you notice **tempo**. If the offense hurries to the line without substituting, the
defense may be stuck with the eleven it has, the
[substitution freeze](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-substitution-freeze) from
[In-Game Adjustments and Tempo](../08-the-chess-match/08-04-in-game-adjustments-and-tempo.qmd). An offense
that goes fast right after a big gain, or right after the defense has subbed into a run-stopping group, is
usually hunting a mismatch it has already spotted.

Why second: personnel is visible before the formation is, and it's the context for everything the formation
shows. As you'll see shortly, it adds surprisingly little to a run-or-pass call on its own. Its value is in
what it sets up.

### Step 3: formation, strength and the offensive tells

This is the richest step. Where is the quarterback: under center, in the shotgun, in the pistol? Where is
the back, how deep, offset to which side? Where is the tight end, on the line or off it, in a three-point
stance or standing up? How wide are the receivers? Which side is the
[formation strength](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-formation-strength)? Part 2 taught the vocabulary,
Parts 3 and 4 the families of plays each look goes with, and [the tells catalogue](#the-tells-catalogue)
below collects every alignment clue in one place.

Why third: the offense has to show its formation before the defense commits to its final picture, and the
defense's last-second picture is a *response* to it. Read the formation first and you'll understand what
the defense does next.

### Step 4: motion response

When a player moves before the snap, watch the defense, not the man in motion. A defender who
[travels](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-travel-man-defender-follows-motion) across the formation with him
suggests man coverage; defenders who [bump](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-bump-defensive-adjustment) a
spot over suggest zone; a safety who [spins](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-spin-safety-rotation-on-motion)
down turns two-high into one-high. That's the
[man/zone indicator](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-man-zone-indicator) from
[Motion and Shifts as Weapons](../02-personnel-and-formations/02-06-motion-and-shifts.qmd). Then ask the
offensive question: is he still moving when the ball is snapped
([motion at the snap](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-motion-at-the-snap))? A jet motion at full speed is a
run threat, or a decoy for one, to that side.

You will get to use this step on most snaps. PFF's charting had a shift or motion on 63.9% of 2025 snaps,
the highest in its series, and every team but the Giants used one on at least half its plays.[^motion]

Why fourth: motion only happens after the offense sets, and its whole point is to make the defense answer
a question before the snap. The answer is a clue for steps 5 to 7.

### Step 5: the box

Count the defenders in the [box](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-box) and compare them with the blockers
([box count](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-box-count)). Six blockers against six defenders is a fair fight
for a run; six against eight means someone will be unblocked, which is why an offense that sees eight
usually throws or checks to a run away from the extra man
([Run Fits and Box Math](../05-defensive-fronts-and-run-defense/05-05-run-fits-and-box-math.qmd)). A light
box (six or fewer) against a shotgun offense is the classic invitation for a run or an
[RPO](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-rpo).

Why fifth: the box isn't final until motion has settled it. Count too early and you'll count a safety who
is about to leave, or miss one who is about to arrive.

### Step 6: the shell

One-high or two-high? Then the details: each safety's depth (13 yards is deep, 8 is down), his width (on the
hash, outside it, in the middle), and any creep in the last seconds of the play clock. This was the spine of
Part 6, and [Disguise, Rotation, and Split-Field Coverage](../06-pass-coverage/06-06-disguise-rotation-and-split-field.qmd)
was about why the shell you see is often not the coverage you get. The league has moved toward showing
two-high: NFL Next Gen Stats measured two-high coverage on 42.0% of dropbacks in 2025, the highest since it
began tracking in 2018.[^twohigh] Two-high before the snap, then, is no longer a tell by itself; the tell is
which of the two safeties is shallower, narrower or moving.

Why sixth: safeties are the last defenders to settle and the most likely to be lying, so you read them as
late as you can.

### Step 7: leverage and depth

Look at the corners: pressed at the line or off at seven yards; on the receiver's inside shoulder or his
outside. [Leverage](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-leverage-inside-outside) tells you what the defender is
protecting and so where his help is: a corner playing outside leverage is giving up the inside because
someone (a safety in the middle, a linebacker underneath) is there to take it. Then the linebackers' depth:
at five or six yards they are playing the run and the short middle; creeping to three, they may be coming;
backing out to eight before the snap on a passing down, they are getting a head start into zone drops.

Why seventh: leverage is the last thing a defense adjusts, and it only makes sense after you know the shell.
An inside-leverage corner with two deep safeties means something different from the same corner with one.

### Step 8: pressure tells

How many defenders are at or near the line, and could any of them drop? Linebackers mugging the A gaps,
a safety or nickel back walked up beside the end, a defensive lineman sitting back on his heels: these are
the [pressure look](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-pressure-look) tells from Part 7. Then the count that
caps everything: **how many players are deep?** Two deep safeties and two off corners leave seven to rush and
cover underneath, and a defense almost never rushes six with only one underneath. Finish with the offense's
side: where is the back, which way will the line slide, where is the
[hot route](../../appendices/glossary.qmd#gl-hot-route)?

Why eighth: pressure looks are deliberately last-second. Defenses walk up late so the offense has as
little time as possible to change its protection, and you get the same late look the quarterback does.

### Step 9: call it, with a number

Say it out loud before the snap: run or pass, and how sure you are. Then, if you have a second left, one
more layer: the coverage family, how many will rush, or where the ball should go. This is the step this
chapter adds, and it gets [its own section](#stated-confidence-putting-a-number-on-it) below. The rule is
simple: the call is made *before* the snap, or it doesn't count.

## What each step is worth

How much does each step actually help? For the run-or-pass call, we can measure it. Charting services
record, for every NFL snap, much of what steps 1 to 5 ask about: the situation, the personnel, the
quarterback's alignment and the number of backs, whether there was motion, whether the offense huddled,
and how many defenders were in the box. (Steps 6 to 8 aren't in public data: nobody charts pre-snap safety
depth or corner leverage for every snap.) So we can do what a reader would do: learn from one season what
each combination of clues usually meant, then call every snap of the next season, adding one step at a time.

```{python}
#| label: fig-checklist-worth
#| fig-cap: "What the measurable steps are worth for a run-or-pass call. Each row adds one checklist step to a model learned on the 2024 regular season and then scored on every 2025 regular-season run and dropback (32,813 snaps). Left: how often the call was right. Right: the share of snaps the model could call at 80% confidence or more, and (in the label) how often those confident calls were right. The situation does most of the work; the formation (quarterback's alignment and number of backs) is the one big jump after it; motion, tempo and the box add almost nothing to run or pass. Source: nflverse play-by-play, FTN charting and participation."
fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(6.5, 2.75), sharey=True, gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1.15, 1]))
names = [w_["step"] for w_ in WORTH]
ys = np.arange(len(names))[::-1]
cols = [style.MUTED] + [style.OFFENSE] * (len(names) - 1)
cols[3] = style.THIRD                          # the formation step: the big jump
accs = [w_["acc"] for w_ in WORTH]
a1.barh(ys, accs, color=cols, height=0.6, zorder=2)
for y_, v in zip(ys, accs):
    a1.text(v + 0.004, y_, pct(v, 1), va="center", ha="left", fontsize=7.4, color=style.INK)
a1.set_xlim(0.55, 0.81)
a1.set_yticks(ys, names, fontsize=7.6)
a1.xaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:.0%}"))
a1.set_xlabel("run/pass calls right, 2025", fontsize=7.6)
a1.set_title("Accuracy", fontsize=8.6)
a1.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
his = [0 if np.isnan(w_["hi"]) else w_["hi"] for w_ in WORTH]
a2.barh(ys, his, color=cols, height=0.6, zorder=2)
for y_, w_ in zip(ys, WORTH):
    if np.isnan(w_["hi"]):
        a2.text(0.01, y_, "never sure", va="center", ha="left", fontsize=7.0, color=style.INK_2, style="italic")
    else:
        a2.text(w_["hi"] + 0.008, y_, f"{pct(w_['hi'])}  ({pct(w_['hi_acc'])} right)", va="center", ha="left",
                fontsize=7.0, color=style.INK)
a2.set_xlim(0, 0.72)
a2.xaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:.0%}"))
a2.set_xlabel("share of snaps called at 80%+", fontsize=7.6)
a2.set_title("Confident calls", fontsize=8.6)
a2.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
fig.tight_layout(w_pad=0.8)
plt.show()
```

Three lessons hide in that chart.[^worth]

**The situation is most of the call.** Down, distance, field zone, score and clock take you from
`{python} pct(W["Always guess pass"]["acc"])` ("always pass") to `{python} pct(W["Situation"]["acc"])`.
That is the step a casual fan skips, because it feels too obvious to count. It isn't obvious; it's just
quick.

**The formation is the one big jump after it.** Adding the quarterback's alignment and the number of backs
lifts the model to `{python} pct(W["+ Formation"]["acc"])`, and, as important, raises the share of snaps it
can call at 80% confidence or better from `{python} pct(W["Situation"]["hi"])` to
`{python} pct(W["+ Formation"]["hi"])`. Personnel alone added little on top of the situation (about
`{python} f"{100 * (W['+ Personnel']['acc'] - W['Situation']['acc']):.1f}"` points), because most of what the personnel
tells you, the formation tells you again, more precisely.

**Motion, tempo and the box add almost nothing to run or pass.** Together they move the needle by
`{python} f"{100 * (W['+ Box count']['acc'] - W['+ Formation']['acc']):.1f}"` points. That isn't because they're useless. It's because they answer *other questions*. Motion
is for identifying the coverage. The box is for knowing whether the run, if it comes, has a chance. And the
defense's box count is partly a reply to the offense's formation, so it repeats what you already knew. The
same is surely true of the steps nobody charts: safety depth and corner leverage tell you little about
*whether* the offense will throw, and a great deal about *where* and *against what*.

That changes how you should spend your twenty seconds. **By the end of step 3 your run-or-pass call is
essentially made. Steps 4 to 8 are for the second layer**: the coverage, the pressure, where the ball should
go, which way the run will hit. A reader who spends all twenty seconds agonising over run or pass is using
the expensive steps on the cheap question.

## The tells catalogue

[How to Watch a Broadcast](../01-foundations/01-06-how-to-watch-a-broadcast.qmd) started a catalogue with four
starter tells (stance, the back's depth and offset, splits, safety depth) and promised the full version here.
This is it: ten clues, five from each side of the ball, and a plate that shows where each one lives.

```{python}
#| label: fig-tells-plate
#| fig-cap: "The tells catalogue on one plate. A shotgun offense with 11 personnel (one back, one tight end) faces a nickel defense with two deep safeties. Numbered badges mark where each tell lives: 1 to 5 on the offense, 6 to 10 on the defense; the key below says what each usually suggests. Every one is a lean, not a guarantee, and some of the alignments drawn here are exaggerated so the clue is visible: the right corner is pressed with inside leverage, the left corner is off with outside leverage, the Mike has crept to three yards, and the right safety is shallower and narrower than his partner."
off = offense("gun_2x2")
OMOVE = {"Y": (-0.7, 4.8), "Z": (-1.5, 10.5), "X": (-0.7, -15.5), "H": (-1.5, -9.0), "RB": (-5.2, 1.7)}
off = [p_.moved(d=OMOVE[p_.key][0], w=OMOVE[p_.key][1]) if p_.key in OMOVE else p_ for p_ in off]
dfn = defense("nickel", "two_high", off)
DMOVE = {"WDE": (1.0, -7.0), "WDT": (1.0, -2.4), "SDT": (1.0, 1.0), "SDE": (1.0, 5.6), "MIKE": (3.0, 1.2),
         "WILL": (5.5, -2.6), "NB": (5.0, -6.3), "LCB": (7.0, -16.6), "RCB": (1.0, 9.8), "FS": (13.5, -9.5),
         "SS": (10.5, 6.0)}
dfn = [p_.moved(d=DMOVE[p_.key][0], w=DMOVE[p_.key][1]) if p_.key in DMOVE else p_ for p_ in dfn]
dfn = [p_.moved(label="CB") if p_.pos == "CB" else p_ for p_ in dfn]
pl = Play(off, dfn, los=40, to_go=None)
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(6.5, 7.15))
axf = fig.add_axes([0.0, 0.40, 1.0, 0.60])
axk = fig.add_axes([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.40])
blank(axk)
fld = pl.draw(ax=axf, lateral=(-24, 24), window=(-8.5, 17.0), title=False)
no_numbers(fld.ax)
for n, at in [(1, (-2.7, 2.4)), (2, (-5.2, 3.6)), (3, (-5.0, -1.9)), (4, (-3.4, 10.5)), (5, (-2.6, 6.2)),
              (6, (2.9, -7.6)), (7, (3.0, 3.1)), (8, (6.9, -7.2)), (9, (2.8, 11.4)), (9, (8.9, -17.4)),
              (10, (10.5, 8.0)), (10, (13.5, -11.6))]:
    fbadge(fld, pl, n, at, r=1.05, fs=6.8)
tag(fld, pl, "hash", (15.5, 3.1), fs=6.0, color=style.INK_2)
tag(fld, pl, "hash", (15.5, -3.1), fs=6.0, color=style.INK_2)
KEY = [
    (1, "Linemen's stance", "Heavy hand, weight forward: run block. Light hand, hips back, a tackle's outside "
        "foot staggered back: pass set."),
    (2, "Back's depth and offset", "Shotgun runs usually go away from the side he's on; deeper than usual wants "
        "room to read a run, closer suggests a block or a quick route."),
    (3, "Shotgun, pistol, under center", "2025 pass rates: shotgun " + pct(RATE["gun"]) + ", pistol "
        + pct(RATE["pistol"]) + ", under center " + pct(RATE["uc"]) + " (and most of those were play-action)."),
    (4, "Receiver split", "Reduced (inside the numbers): a crack block, a short crosser, or room to break "
        "outside. Wide: isolated, a deep or in-breaking route."),
    (5, "Tight end's stance", "Hand down, in line: usually a block (or a release that looks like one). Standing, "
        "flexed off the line: usually a route."),
    (6, "Lineman's width and stance", "A wide edge rusher is built to rush the passer; a lineman back on his "
        "heels may be stunting or dropping."),
    (7, "Linebacker depth", "At 5–6 yards: the run and the short middle. Creeping to 3 late: blitz or a run "
        "fit. Backing out before the snap: a zone drop."),
    (8, "Nickel's spot", "Apexed between the box and the slot: run support or a zone. Walked up and tight on the "
        "slot: man, or a nickel blitz."),
    (9, "Corner depth and leverage", "Pressed: man or a hard corner. Off and outside: help is inside. Inside "
        "leverage: help is over the top or outside."),
    (10, "Safety depth and width", "Deep and on or outside the hash: a deep half or quarter. Shallower, "
         "narrower or moving: the one about to rotate or come down."),
]
axk.set_xlim(0, 100)
axk.set_ylim(0, 100)
axk.text(2.5, 97.5, "Offense", fontsize=8.5, fontweight="bold", color=style.OFFENSE_DARK, va="center")
axk.text(52.5, 97.5, "Defense", fontsize=8.5, fontweight="bold", color=style.DEFENSE_DARK, va="center")
for i_, (n, title, txt) in enumerate(KEY):
    col = 0 if n <= 5 else 1
    row = (n - 1) % 5
    x0 = 2.5 + 50 * col
    y0 = 89.5 - row * 19.0
    axk.scatter([x0 + 1.4], [y0], s=125, color=LOOK, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.8, zorder=5)
    axk.text(x0 + 1.4, y0, str(n), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=6.0 if n < 10 else 5.4, color="white",
             fontweight="bold", zorder=6)
    axk.text(x0 + 4.4, y0, title, ha="left", va="center", fontsize=7.4, fontweight="bold", color=style.INK)
    axk.text(x0 + 4.4, y0 - 3.4, "\n".join(textwrap.wrap(txt, 64)), ha="left", va="top", fontsize=6.5,
             color=style.INK_2, linespacing=1.12)
```
